title: Logarithmic differentiation and variable powers
section: The Natural Exponential and Logarithm Functions ▷ Variable exponents
terms: logarithmic differentiation; variable exponent; logarithmic derivative; exponential rewrit- ing.

For positive u(x) and differentiable v(x), write u(x) = exp(v(x) log u(x)). Differentiation

change of base; the ordinary power rule only covers constant exponents.
For a nonzero differentiable product or quotient, differentiating log |f| often turns multiplica-
′
tion into addition and division into subtraction. Recover f by multiplying the logarithmic
derivative by f. Real variable powers require positive bases unless a special domain has been
explicitly justified. Logarithmic differentiation can also identify critical points of a positive
function using the simpler derivative of its logarithm.
The same method applies to implicit equations with positive variable powers: take logarithms
on both sides before differentiating, and include the derivative of every dependent variable. To
classify an extremum of a positive function, the sign of its logarithmic derivative is the sign of
its ordinary derivative.
